nghi_van.mo_ta: A boxy, dark green, car-like vehicle with a flat roof and glazed windows stands in the street background. It looks like an early motor car or a closed motor van.
nghi_van.ly_do: Motor vehicles did not exist in 1667. Street traffic was horse-drawn carts, sedan chairs and coaches, and a boxy glazed body like this does not match any of them.

tra_loi.vat: A boxy, enclosed motor car, possibly an early-1900s automobile or taxi
tra_loi.dac_diem: A dark green-grey square cabin with a flat roof that overhangs slightly. It has a rectangular window at the front and a side window. The body is upright and boxy, and it sits in a street among pedestrians and a horse. It is blurry, so I can't see wheels or other detail.
tra_loi.ly_do: The enclosed, flat-roofed motorcar body is a design from the early 20th century. In 1667 London had only horse-drawn coaches, sedan chairs and carts, with no motor vehicles.

nghi_van.mo_ta: Bricklayers wear soft flat peaked caps (newsboy or baker-boy style) with a stitched crown and short brim. They also wear fitted waistcoats over collarless shirts.
nghi_van.ly_do: The peaked flat cap is a 19th-century working-class style. Workmen in 1667 London would wear brimmed felt hats, knitted or woollen caps, or coifs.

tra_loi.vat: Flat cap (soft peaked cap) worn by a man
tra_loi.dac_diem: Grey, soft, rounded crown that looks paneled or stitched, with a short stiff brim at the front. It sits low on the head of a bearded man. He wears a grey waistcoat or vest over a rolled-sleeve off-white shirt. A brick wall and a dark doorway are behind him. The image is blurry, so the seams and stitching are not clearly visible.
tra_loi.ly_do: The wool flat caps of the 16th and 17th centuries were brimless soft bonnets. A flat or newsboy cap with a sewn crown and a stiff peak became common in the 19th century, especially in the late 1800s. This design is therefore probably anachronistic for London in 1667. The blur leaves some uncertainty.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A bricklayer on the scaffold at top right wears a flat peaked cap and a Victorian-style waistcoat.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The peaked flat cap and the tailored waistcoat are 19th-century workwear, not 1660s dress.
